sentence: ___ the noise from the road, we slept well.
setupText: Choose the connector that fits the noun phrase and presents the noise as an obstacle overcome.
taskText: ___ the noise from the road, we slept well.
text: Choose the connector that fits the noun phrase and presents the noise as an obstacle overcome. ___ the noise from the road, we slept well.
explanation: Despite takes the noun phrase and marks the unexpected success of sleeping well.

rationales.Although: Although needs a clause here, such as although the road was noisy.
rationales.Because of: Because of would make the noise a reason for sleeping well, not an obstacle overcome.
rationales.Despite: Despite takes the noun phrase and marks the unexpected success of sleeping well.
rationales.Since: Since does not directly introduce this noun phrase as a conceded obstacle.

sentence: The meeting did not start ___ the interpreter arrived.
setupText: Choose the phrase meaning the meeting started only when the interpreter arrived.
taskText: The meeting did not start ___ the interpreter arrived.
text: Choose the phrase meaning the meeting started only when the interpreter arrived. The meeting did not start ___ the interpreter arrived.
explanation: Not ... until postpones the start to the interpreter's arrival.

rationales.although: Although contrasts facts rather than identifying the first possible starting point.
rationales.until: Not ... until postpones the start to the interpreter's arrival.
rationales.because: Because would make arrival the reason the meeting failed to start.
rationales.while: While describes overlapping time rather than the endpoint of the delay.

sentence: I prefer working alone, ___ my colleague enjoys a busy team office.
setupText: Choose the connector comparing two different preferences, without expressing cause or timing.
taskText: I prefer working alone, ___ my colleague enjoys a busy team office.
text: Choose the connector comparing two different preferences, without expressing cause or timing. I prefer working alone, ___ my colleague enjoys a busy team office.
explanation: Whereas contrasts the two people's working preferences.

rationales.because: Because would make the colleague's preference a reason for yours.
rationales.until: Until creates a time boundary that is not part of the comparison.
rationales.so that: So that would make the colleague's enjoyment the purpose of your preference.
rationales.whereas: Whereas contrasts the two people's working preferences.

sentence: 'Since the shop has no spare parts, we'll try another repair service.'
setupText: Choose the meaning of 'since' in this message.
taskText: 'Since the shop has no spare parts, we'll try another repair service.'
text: Choose the meaning of 'since' in this message. 'Since the shop has no spare parts, we'll try another repair service.'
options: From the time the shop opened.
Until the shop receives spare parts.
Despite the shop having no spare parts.
Because the shop has no spare parts.
answer: Because the shop has no spare parts.
explanation: 'Since' introduces the reason for trying a different service here.

'Since' introduces the reason for trying a different service here.
The clause states a current reason, not a starting date.
'Until' would make receiving parts an endpoint rather than give the reason for changing services.
'Despite' makes the lack of parts an obstacle overcome, not the cause of changing services.

sentence: ___ the announcement began, everyone had found a seat.
setupText: Choose the phrase showing that the passengers were already seated when the announcement began.
taskText: ___ the announcement began, everyone had found a seat.
text: Choose the phrase showing that the passengers were already seated when the announcement began. ___ the announcement began, everyone had found a seat.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b1-525:By the time with prior completion
explanation: By the time locates finding seats before or at the later reference point, the announcement's start.

rationales.As long as: As long as introduces a condition or duration, not the required already-completed relationship.
rationales.Even though: Even though introduces concession rather than the requested timing.
rationales.By the time: By the time locates finding seats before or at the later reference point, the announcement's start.
rationales.In order that: In order that introduces purpose, which reverses the relationship between these events.

sentence: The cafe stayed open ___ there were only two customers.
setupText: Choose the completion that forms a clause expressing concession.
taskText: The cafe stayed open ___ there were only two customers.
text: Choose the completion that forms a clause expressing concession. The cafe stayed open ___ there were only two customers.
explanation: Although introduces the complete clause describing an obstacle to staying open.

rationales.despite: Despite needs a noun or -ing phrase here, not the unintroduced full clause there were.
rationales.although: Although introduces the complete clause describing an obstacle to staying open.
rationales.because of: Because of requires a noun phrase and would express reason rather than concession.
rationales.in spite of: In spite of also needs a noun or -ing phrase, such as in spite of having few customers.

sentence: The instructions were ___ unclear that I called the help desk.
setupText: Choose the completion forming a degree-and-result pattern.
taskText: The instructions were ___ unclear that I called the help desk.
text: Choose the completion forming a degree-and-result pattern. The instructions were ___ unclear that I called the help desk.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b1-527:So ... that for degree and result
explanation: So + adjective + that expresses a degree of unclearness leading to the call.

rationales.such: Such normally introduces a noun phrase, such as such unclear instructions.
rationales.too: Too normally leads to a to-infinitive result, not this that-clause.
rationales.enough: Enough follows the adjective and does not form enough unclear that.
rationales.so: So + adjective + that expresses a degree of unclearness leading to the call.

sentence: It was ___ a long queue that we missed the start of the film.
setupText: Choose the completion forming a natural degree-and-result sentence.
taskText: It was ___ a long queue that we missed the start of the film.
text: Choose the completion forming a natural degree-and-result sentence. It was ___ a long queue that we missed the start of the film.
explanation: Such + a + adjective + noun can be followed by that and a result.

rationales.such: Such + a + adjective + noun can be followed by that and a result.
rationales.so: So cannot directly precede a long queue in this pattern; use such a long queue.
rationales.too: Too does not form too a long queue that.
rationales.enough: Enough would follow a noun or adjective in a different structure, not precede a here.

sentence: I put my phone on silent ___ wake my partner.
setupText: Choose the phrase that expresses a deliberate purpose of avoiding disturbance.
taskText: I put my phone on silent ___ wake my partner.
text: Choose the phrase that expresses a deliberate purpose of avoiding disturbance. I put my phone on silent ___ wake my partner.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b1-529:Negative purpose with in order not to
explanation: In order not to plus wake expresses the intended prevention of an unwanted action.

rationales.because I didn't: Because I didn't gives an actual reason about not waking, not the purpose of setting the phone.
rationales.even though I didn't: Even though I didn't states a concession rather than an intended precaution.
rationales.in order not to: In order not to plus wake expresses the intended prevention of an unwanted action.
rationales.in order to: Without not, this gives waking the partner as the purpose, reversing the intended precaution.

sentence: The menu was in a language we didn't know. We managed to order a good meal.
setupText: Choose the sentence presenting the language difficulty as a fact that did not prevent success.
taskText: The menu was in a language we didn't know. We managed to order a good meal.
text: Choose the sentence presenting the language difficulty as a fact that did not prevent success. The menu was in a language we didn't know. We managed to order a good meal.
options: Even though we couldn't read the menu, we ordered a good meal.
We ordered a good meal because we couldn't read the menu.
We couldn't read the menu so that we could order a good meal.
We could read the menu, so we ordered a good meal.
answer: Even though we couldn't read the menu, we ordered a good meal.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b1-530:Conceding an actual obstacle with even though
explanation: Even though concedes the actual difficulty and contrasts it with the successful result.

rationales.We ordered a good meal because we couldn: Because would make not understanding the menu a cause of the successful order.
rationales.Even though we couldn't read the menu, w: Even though concedes the actual difficulty and contrasts it with the successful result.
rationales.We couldn't read the menu so that we cou: So that turns the difficulty into a deliberate means to achieve a purpose.
rationales.We could read the menu, so we ordered a: This changes the stated inability to read into an ability and makes it the cause of success.

sentence: The bridge was closed for repairs. ___, delivery drivers had to use a longer route.
setupText: Choose the connector introducing a consequence.
taskText: The bridge was closed for repairs. ___, delivery drivers had to use a longer route.
text: Choose the connector introducing a consequence. The bridge was closed for repairs. ___, delivery drivers had to use a longer route.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b1-531:Consequently links cause and outcome across sentences
explanation: Consequently marks the detour as a result of the bridge closure.

rationales.Nevertheless: Nevertheless would present the longer route as an unexpected contrast rather than a consequence.
rationales.For instance: For instance would make the drivers' route an example of the bridge closure, rather than a result of it.
rationales.Meanwhile: Meanwhile only places events at the same time and does not express the requested causal link.
rationales.Consequently: Consequently marks the detour as a result of the bridge closure.

sentence: The chef prepared the food in the kitchen. ___, the servers arranged tables outside.
setupText: Choose the connector showing that a second activity was happening at the same time elsewhere.
taskText: The chef prepared the food in the kitchen. ___, the servers arranged tables outside.
text: Choose the connector showing that a second activity was happening at the same time elsewhere. The chef prepared the food in the kitchen. ___, the servers arranged tables outside.
explanation: Meanwhile links activities occurring during the same period in different places.

rationales.Meanwhile: Meanwhile links activities occurring during the same period in different places.
rationales.Afterwards: Afterwards would put arranging the tables later than the food preparation.
rationales.Therefore: Therefore adds a causal conclusion rather than merely indicating simultaneous activity.
rationales.Instead: Instead would make table arranging replace food preparation, rather than accompany it.

sentence: The train fare is more than I can afford. ___, I have to work that weekend.
setupText: Choose the word adding a second reason for declining the invitation.
taskText: The train fare is more than I can afford. ___, I have to work that weekend.
text: Choose the word adding a second reason for declining the invitation. The train fare is more than I can afford. ___, I have to work that weekend.
explanation: Besides adds the work commitment as a further reason for not going.

rationales.Instead: Instead introduces a replacement, not another reason to decline.
rationales.Otherwise: Otherwise introduces a consequence of a different situation, not an additional obstacle.
rationales.Besides: Besides adds the work commitment as a further reason for not going.
rationales.Nevertheless: Nevertheless introduces a contrast against the first reason, rather than reinforcing it.

sentence: The new packaging uses less plastic. ___, it takes up less space in storage.
setupText: Choose the connector adding another benefit of the same design.
taskText: The new packaging uses less plastic. ___, it takes up less space in storage.
text: Choose the connector adding another benefit of the same design. The new packaging uses less plastic. ___, it takes up less space in storage.
explanation: Moreover adds a further advantage supporting the same positive evaluation.

rationales.Nevertheless: Nevertheless would contrast the storage benefit with the first benefit.
rationales.Moreover: Moreover adds a further advantage supporting the same positive evaluation.
rationales.Instead: Instead would replace the plastic reduction with the space saving.
rationales.Otherwise: Otherwise would introduce an alternative condition or consequence, not another benefit.

sentence: The beach was crowded. We enjoyed the day, ___.
setupText: Choose the word that can stand at the end to express contrast in ordinary conversation.
taskText: The beach was crowded. We enjoyed the day, ___.
text: Choose the word that can stand at the end to express contrast in ordinary conversation. The beach was crowded. We enjoyed the day, ___.
explanation: Sentence-final though means however here and contrasts enjoyment with the crowds.

rationales.although: Although introduces a clause and cannot function alone as this final contrast marker.
rationales.even though: Even though also needs a following clause rather than standing alone at the end.
rationales.despite: Despite needs a complement, such as despite the crowds.
rationales.though: Sentence-final though means however here and contrasts enjoyment with the crowds.

sentence: We went for a walk ___ ordering dessert.
setupText: Choose the phrase expressing a substitute activity.
taskText: We went for a walk ___ ordering dessert.
text: Choose the phrase expressing a substitute activity. We went for a walk ___ ordering dessert.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b1-536:Instead of versus addition, reason and concession
explanation: Instead of makes walking replace ordering dessert.

rationales.instead of: Instead of makes walking replace ordering dessert.
rationales.as well as: As well as adds walking to dessert, implying both activities rather than substitution.
rationales.because of: Because of makes ordering dessert the cause of the walk.
rationales.in spite of: In spite of treats ordering dessert as an obstacle that did not prevent the walk.

sentence: I don't know whether he slept. He looked ___ he hadn't slept all night.
setupText: Choose the connector describing an appearance without confirming its cause.
taskText: I don't know whether he slept. He looked ___ he hadn't slept all night.
text: Choose the connector describing an appearance without confirming its cause. I don't know whether he slept. He looked ___ he hadn't slept all night.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b1-537:As if for an unconfirmed appearance
explanation: As if compares his appearance with that of someone who had not slept, without confirming it happened.

rationales.because: Because would assert lack of sleep as the reason, which the speaker does not know.
rationales.so that: So that would make not sleeping the purpose or result of looking a certain way.
rationales.as if: As if compares his appearance with that of someone who had not slept, without confirming it happened.
rationales.even though: Even though would concede lack of sleep as a fact and suggest a contrast.

sentence: The system sends a receipt ___ I renew my membership.
setupText: Choose the connector meaning every time the action happens.
taskText: The system sends a receipt ___ I renew my membership.
text: Choose the connector meaning every time the action happens. The system sends a receipt ___ I renew my membership.
explanation: Whenever means on every occasion that the membership is renewed.

rationales.until: Until marks an endpoint for sending, not a receipt for each renewal.
rationales.whenever: Whenever means on every occasion that the membership is renewed.
rationales.although: Although introduces a contrast and does not express repeated timing.
rationales.once before: Once before describes a single earlier occasion rather than every renewal.

sentence: 'I haven't seen the old shop owner since she moved away.'
setupText: Choose the interpretation of 'since' in this sentence.
taskText: 'I haven't seen the old shop owner since she moved away.'
text: Choose the interpretation of 'since' in this sentence. 'I haven't seen the old shop owner since she moved away.'
options: The move marks the beginning of the period without a meeting.
Moving away is presented as the only reason for not meeting.
Seeing the owner happened at the same time as the move.
The speaker expects to see the owner before she moves.
answer: The move marks the beginning of the period without a meeting.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b1-539:Temporal since after a negative present perfect
explanation: 'Since' links the past move to the continuing period in which no meeting has occurred.

rationales.Moving away is presented as the only rea: The sentence's present-perfect time structure locates a starting event; it does not specify an exclusive cause.
rationales.Seeing the owner happened at the same ti: The negative says there has been no meeting in the period following the move.
rationales.The speaker expects to see the owner bef: 'Moved away' is a past event, not a future move awaiting a meeting.
rationales.The move marks the beginning of the peri: 'Since' links the past move to the continuing period in which no meeting has occurred.

sentence: The hotel already offered free parking. This existing service persuaded us to book.
setupText: Choose the sentence that gives a confirmed benefit as the reason for the choice, rather than stating a goal.
taskText: The hotel already offered free parking. This existing service persuaded us to book.
text: Choose the sentence that gives a confirmed benefit as the reason for the choice, rather than stating a goal. The hotel already offered free parking. This existing service persuaded us to book.
options: We booked the hotel so that we could park there for free.
We booked the hotel because we could park there for free.
We booked the hotel although we could park there for free.
We booked the hotel until we could park there for free.
answer: We booked the hotel because we could park there for free.
explanation: Because presents the confirmed parking service as the reason that motivated the booking.

rationales.We booked the hotel because we could par: Because presents the confirmed parking service as the reason that motivated the booking.
rationales.We booked the hotel so that we could par: So that expresses the intended purpose of booking rather than explicitly giving the established benefit as a reason.
rationales.We booked the hotel although we could pa: Although contrasts the parking benefit with booking, contrary to its motivating role.
rationales.We booked the hotel until we could park: Until makes parking an endpoint of a booking period rather than the reason for choosing the hotel.
